glossary.Nasal cavity: The air space inside the nose, behind the nostrils.
glossary.Facial pain: Pain over the cheeks, forehead or between the eyes, from pressure in blocked sinuses.
glossary.Nasal congestion: Blocked or stuffy nose from swollen lining.
glossary.Purulent nasal discharge: Thick, coloured (yellow or green) mucus containing pus from the nose.
glossary.Neurological signs: Examination findings showing nervous system involvement, such as weakness, confusion or altered consciousness.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Anti-inflammatory steroid drugs, such as prednisolone, or fluticasone as a nasal spray.
glossary.Oral corticosteroids: Steroid tablets, such as prednisolone, taken by mouth.
glossary.Penicillin allergic: Having had an allergic reaction to penicillin, so penicillin-type antibiotics must be avoided.
glossary.Stasis: Stagnation of fluid that is not flowing or draining.
glossary.Secondary bacterial infection: Bacterial infection that takes hold after an earlier viral illness has damaged the tissue.
glossary.Skull base: The floor of the skull on which the brain sits, bordering the sinuses below.
glossary.Cranial cavity: The space inside the skull that holds the brain.
glossary.Severe headache: An intense headache that can signal spread of infection inside the skull.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used for pain, fever and inflammation.
glossary.Mucosal inflammation: Swelling and irritation of the moist lining of the nose and sinuses.
glossary.Viral: Caused by a virus; antibiotics do not help.
glossary.ENT referral: Sending the patient to an ear, nose and throat specialist.
